items.stem: Define the term 'target audience'.
items.answer: The group of people that an ICT solution, such as a website or presentation, is designed for.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: The group of people that an ICT solution, such as a website or presentation, is designed for. [2]

items.stem: Explain why it is important to identify the target audience before designing a website.
items.answer: The content, language, layout, colours and level of detail must suit the users' age, knowledge and needs; otherwise they may not understand it or may lose interest.
items.markingKey: 1 mark design must match audience; 1 mark consequence of not doing so. [2]

items.stem: Explain two ways a website could be designed for elderly users.
items.answer: Larger font sizes and high contrast for reduced eyesight; simple navigation with clear buttons; avoid jargon; option for audio.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark feature, 1 mark reason). [4]

items.stem: Tomás is creating a multimedia presentation for Vista Estate Agents in Karachi to show to primary school children. Explain why the solution should be tested with members of the target audience.
items.answer: They can show whether it meets their needs and is easy to use, so problems can be fixed before release.
items.markingKey: 1 mark feedback on suitability; 1 mark changes made before release. [2]

items.stem: Starlight Cinemas in Lima is designing a website to sell holidays to people over 65. (a) Describe how the designer could find out what the audience needs. (b) Explain why the solution should be tested with members of the target audience.
items.answer: (a) Questionnaires; interviews; focus groups; testing prototypes with users. (b) They can show whether it meets their needs and is easy to use, so problems can be fixed before release.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark method; 1 mark description. [2] (b) 1 mark feedback on suitability; 1 mark changes made before release. [2]

items.stem: TransGlobal Logistics in Singapore wants an app that helps new employees learn company procedures. Assess the importance of audience appreciation in the success of the solution for TransGlobal Logistics.
items.answer: Points for: a solution matched to users is easier to use, more engaging and more likely to be adopted. Points against / limitations: research takes time and money; audiences are varied so one design cannot suit everyone; good content also matters. Conclusion: audience appreciation is essential, though designers must balance it against budget and the needs of different groups.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks points developed and applied with a conclusion. Indicative content — for: a solution matched to users is easier to use, more engaging and more likely to be adopted. Against: research takes time and money; audiences are varied so one design cannot suit everyone; good content also matters. Conclusion may argue: audience appreciation is essential, though designers must balance it against budget and the needs of different groups. [4]

items.stem: Define the term 'digital divide'.
items.answer: The gap between people who have access to, and can use, modern information and communication technology and those who do not.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: The gap between people who have access to, and can use, modern information and communication technology and those who do not. [2]

items.stem: Explain two causes of the digital divide.
items.answer: Cost: low-income households cannot afford devices or connection; infrastructure: rural or developing areas lack broadband/electricity; skills: lack of digital literacy, especially among older people; language or disability barriers.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark cause, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Explain how the digital divide can affect a person's job prospects.
items.answer: Many jobs are advertised and applied for online and need IT skills; people without access or skills miss opportunities and are less employable.
items.markingKey: 1 mark online applications/IT skills needed; 1 mark disadvantage. [2]

items.stem: Nova Telecom in Dubai wants to understand why some of its customers do not use its online services. Describe two causes of the digital divide in this situation.
items.answer: Cost of devices and connection; lack of infrastructure in rural areas; lack of skills/digital literacy; age; disability; language.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each, max 2. [2]

items.stem: Zara is writing an article for SkyLink Airways about the digital divide in and around Istanbul. (a) Describe two causes of the digital divide in this situation. (b) Explain one effect of the digital divide on the economy of the area.
items.answer: (a) Cost of devices and connection; lack of infrastructure in rural areas; lack of skills/digital literacy; age; disability; language. (b) Businesses are less competitive and investment goes elsewhere, so there are fewer jobs and lower growth.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each, max 2. [2] (b) 1 mark effect; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Jonas is writing an article for Vista Estate Agents about the digital divide in and around Istanbul. Discuss whether the digital divide is mainly caused by cost rather than by lack of skills.

Points against / limitations: many people with access lack skills or confidence; age, disability and language also matter; some choose not to use ICT. Conclusion: cost and skills both matter; the main cause varies between groups and places.

items.stem: Isla is writing an article for Starlight Cinemas about the digital divide in and around Accra. (a) Describe two causes of the digital divide in this situation. (b) Explain two effects of the digital divide on individuals.
items.answer: (a) Cost of devices and connection; lack of infrastructure in rural areas; lack of skills/digital literacy; age; disability; language. (b) Fewer job opportunities; less access to online education and services; social isolation; paying more without online deals.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each, max 2. [2] (b) 2 × (1 mark effect, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Which accessibility feature helps a deaf user watch an online lecture?
options: Voice recognition
Captions (subtitles)
A screen magnifier
A screen reader
items.answer: Captions (subtitles)
items.markingKey: Captions (subtitles). Captions show the spoken words as text.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Raising broadband prices reduces the digital divide. Reason (R): People who cannot afford a computer can still use the internet. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is false but R is true
items.markingKey: A is false: "Raising broadband prices reduces the digital divide." is incorrect; R is a true statement.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Captions on videos improve accessibility. Reason (R): Deaf users can read what is being said. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A is true and R explains why A is true.

items.stem: The council in Riyadh and Kestrel Architects are working together to reduce the digital divide and make online services accessible. Explain why training is needed as well as providing equipment.
items.answer: People without digital skills or confidence will not use equipment effectively, so access alone does not close the divide.
items.markingKey: 1 mark skills gap; 1 mark consequence. [2]

items.stem: The council in Toronto and Lotus Fashion are working together to reduce the digital divide and make online services accessible. (a) Describe two initiatives that could reduce the digital divide. (b) Describe two accessibility features that should be included.
items.answer: (a) Rural broadband investment; free public internet access points; subsidised devices; digital skills training; low-cost data plans. (b) Alt text for images; captions; resizable text; high contrast; keyboard navigation; compatibility with screen readers; voice input.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each, max 2. [2] (b) 1 mark each, max 2. [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) State what is meant by 'audience appreciation'. (b) Explain what is meant by the term 'accessibility'.
items.answer: (a) Planning and designing a solution by considering the age, knowledge, interests, needs and abilities of the people who will use it. (b) How easily a product can be used by people with different abilities, including people with disabilities.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: Planning and designing a solution by considering the age, knowledge, interests, needs and abilities of the people who will use it. [2] (b) 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: How easily a product can be used by people with different abilities, including people with disabilities. [2]

items.stem: Describe the difference between 'target audience' and 'accessibility'.
items.answer: target audience: The group of people that an ICT solution, such as a website or presentation, is designed for. accessibility: How easily a product can be used by people with different abilities, including people with disabilities.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: target audience correctly described; 1 mark: accessibility correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Assertion (A): A presentation for experts can use technical vocabulary. Reason (R): The audience already understands the subject. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A is true and R explains why A is true.

items.stem: Sunrise Bakery in Accra is creating a website for international tourists. Describe two design features that would suit this audience.
items.answer: Multiple language options, icons and maps, simple vocabulary.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each feature with brief justification, e.g. multiple language options, icons and maps, simple vocabulary. [2]

items.stem: SkyLink Airways in Dubai is designing a website to sell holidays to people over 65. Describe how the designer could find out what the audience needs.
items.answer: Questionnaires; interviews; focus groups; testing prototypes with users.
items.markingKey: 1 mark method; 1 mark description. [2]

items.stem: Silverline Couriers in Istanbul wants an app that helps new employees learn company procedures. (a) Describe how the designer could find out what the audience needs. (b) Explain why the solution should be tested with members of the target audience.
items.answer: (a) Questionnaires; interviews; focus groups; testing prototypes with users. (b) They can show whether it meets their needs and is easy to use, so problems can be fixed before release.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark method; 1 mark description. [2] (b) 1 mark feedback on suitability; 1 mark changes made before release. [2]

items.stem: Eagles Sports Club in Jakarta wants an app that helps new employees learn company procedures. (a) Describe how the designer could find out what the audience needs. (b) Explain why the solution should be tested with members of the target audience.
items.answer: (a) Questionnaires; interviews; focus groups; testing prototypes with users. (b) They can show whether it meets their needs and is easy to use, so problems can be fixed before release.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark method; 1 mark description. [2] (b) 1 mark feedback on suitability; 1 mark changes made before release. [2]

items.stem: Sipho is creating a multimedia presentation for FreshFarm Foods in Riyadh to show to primary school children. Evaluate the importance of audience appreciation in the success of the solution for FreshFarm Foods.
items.answer: Points for: a solution matched to users is easier to use, more engaging and more likely to be adopted. Points against / limitations: research takes time and money; audiences are varied so one design cannot suit everyone; good content also matters. Conclusion: audience appreciation is essential, though designers must balance it against budget and the needs of different groups.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks developed points on one or both sides; 5-6 marks balanced, applied discussion with a justified conclusion. Indicative content — for: a solution matched to users is easier to use, more engaging and more likely to be adopted. Against: research takes time and money; audiences are varied so one design cannot suit everyone; good content also matters. Conclusion may argue: audience appreciation is essential, though designers must balance it against budget and the needs of different groups. [6]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) State what is meant by 'digital literacy'. (b) Explain what is meant by the term 'infrastructure (in ICT)'.
items.answer: (a) The skills needed to find, evaluate, use and create information using digital technology. (b) The physical systems, such as broadband cables, mobile masts and electricity supply, needed for people to access ICT.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: The skills needed to find, evaluate, use and create information using digital technology. [2] (b) 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: The physical systems, such as broadband cables, mobile masts and electricity supply, needed for people to access ICT. [2]

items.stem: Distinguish between 'infrastructure (in ICT)' and 'digital literacy'.
items.answer: infrastructure (in ICT): The physical systems, such as broadband cables, mobile masts and electricity supply, needed for people to access ICT. digital literacy: The skills needed to find, evaluate, use and create information using digital technology.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: infrastructure (in ICT) correctly described; 1 mark: digital literacy correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Assertion (A): People without internet access may pay more for some goods and services. Reason (R): The digital divide only exists between countries. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is true but R is false
items.markingKey: A is true; R is false: "The digital divide only exists between countries." is incorrect.

items.stem: A survey in a region near Istanbul found that 93% of high-income households and 41% of rural households have home broadband access. Calculate the gap in access in percentage points. There are 120,000 rural households in the region. Calculate how many of them do not have broadband access.
items.answer: 52 percentage points; 70,800 rural households without access

items.stem: A government report on the region around Mexico City says that many households still have no internet access. Explain one effect of the digital divide on the economy of the area.
items.answer: Businesses are less competitive and investment goes elsewhere, so there are fewer jobs and lower growth.
items.markingKey: 1 mark effect; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: A survey in a region near Dhaka found that 46% of low-income households and 94% of households aged 16-34 have home broadband access. Calculate the gap in access in percentage points. There are 120,000 low-income households in the region. Calculate how many of them do not have broadband access. Suggest two reasons for the difference between the two groups.
items.answer: 48 percentage points; 64,800 low-income households without access; reasons: e.g. cost of devices/connection, weaker infrastructure, lack of skills
items.markingKey: gap = 94 − 46 = 48 percentage points [1]; 120,000 × 54% = 64,800 [1]; reasons such as cost, infrastructure/coverage, skills, age, interest [2]. [4]

items.stem: Starlight Cinemas in Bangkok wants to understand why some of its customers do not use its online services. Discuss whether the digital divide is mainly caused by cost rather than by lack of skills.
items.answer: Points for: devices and data plans are unaffordable for low-income households; infrastructure costs money. Points against / limitations: many people with access lack skills or confidence; age, disability and language also matter; some choose not to use ICT. Conclusion: cost and skills both matter; the main cause varies between groups and places.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks developed points on one or both sides; 5-6 marks balanced, applied discussion with a justified conclusion. Indicative content — for: devices and data plans are unaffordable for low-income households; infrastructure costs money. Against: many people with access lack skills or confidence; age, disability and language also matter; some choose not to use ICT. Conclusion may argue: cost and skills both matter; the main cause varies between groups and places. [6]

items.stem: Which initiative most directly tackles the cost cause of the digital divide?
options: Making websites more colourful
Building faster supercomputers
Providing subsidised or free devices and data to low-income families
Increasing the price of broadband
items.answer: Providing subsidised or free devices and data to low-income families
items.markingKey: Providing subsidised or free devices and data to low-income families. Reducing cost increases access for poorer households.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Captions on videos improve accessibility. Reason (R): Screen readers are designed for deaf users. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: A is true but R is false
items.markingKey: A is true; R is false: "Screen readers are designed for deaf users." is incorrect.

items.stem: Assertion (A): Captions on videos improve accessibility. Reason (R): People who cannot afford a computer can still use the internet. Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
items.markingKey: A and R are both true statements, but R does not explain A.

items.stem: Peak Fitness in Bangkok wants its online services to be available and accessible to everyone in the region. Describe two initiatives that could reduce the digital divide.
items.answer: Rural broadband investment; free public internet access points; subsidised devices; digital skills training; low-cost data plans.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each, max 2. [2]

items.stem: TransGlobal Logistics in Istanbul wants its online services to be available and accessible to everyone in the region. Evaluate whether providing free devices is the most effective way to reduce the digital divide.
items.answer: Points for: removes the cost barrier immediately; helps students and job seekers. Points against / limitations: devices are useless without connectivity and skills; devices become outdated; may be sold; infrastructure and training may have more lasting impact. Conclusion: a combined programme of infrastructure, devices and skills training is more effective than devices alone.
items.markingKey: Levels marking: 1-2 marks basic points; 3-4 marks points developed and applied with a conclusion. Indicative content — for: removes the cost barrier immediately; helps students and job seekers. Against: devices are useless without connectivity and skills; devices become outdated; may be sold; infrastructure and training may have more lasting impact. Conclusion may argue: a combined programme of infrastructure, devices and skills training is more effective than devices alone. [4]
